meta.purpose: Ledger of specific news claims the nightly scanner has already verified as misdated (the underlying event is real, but its true date is a year or more away from the date implied by the aggregator/republication that surfaced it). Created for backlog item SC-1 / defect class DC-13, opened after the Meta '8,000 layoffs' claim and the China 'Ethnic Unity Law' claim each recurred and were re-verified from scratch across multiple nightly cycles, and after 8 of the 14 candidates dropped on the 2026-09-18 cycle turned out to be the same shape of error.
meta.brief_addendum: Before verifying a candidate's date from scratch, check research/known-misdated-claims.json for an active entry matching this entity. If one matches, you do not need to re-run verification searches -- cite the entry's true_date and source, drop the candidate as already-known, and append today's date to that entry's occurrences[] array (append-only; do not edit or remove prior entries). An entry means 'this specific claim is misdated', not 'this entity is banned' -- the same entity can and will produce genuine, correctly-dated news on a different topic, and that must still be flagged normally. validate-scan.mjs enforces this: it fails the scan if a top_entities candidate matches an active ledger entry's matcher, but a correctly-dropped candidate never triggers a failure.
meta.how_entries_are_read: See research/scripts/validate-scan.mjs, section 8 (checkKnownMisdatedClaims). Only entries with status 'active' are checked. A candidate is flagged when EVERY token-group in matcher[] has at least one substring hit (case-insensitive) against the concatenated slug+name+news_summary text of a research/scans/<date>.json top_entities item.

claims.description: 'Meta cuts/lays off 8,000 jobs' is a real event, but it happened 2026-05-20, not in September. An undated aggregator snippet keeps getting re-surfaced as if it were new.
claims.claimed_framing: Implies the 8,000-job cut is a fresh September 2026 announcement/execution.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the Meta entity token AND the specific 8,000 headcount figure AND a job/layoff word, all three, regardless of phrasing order (e.g. 'cut 8,000 jobs' and '8,000 job cuts' both match). A genuine, differently-sized Meta layoff (e.g. 12,000 jobs) or a genuine Meta story with no layoff/job content will not match, because at least one required group is absent. The count group (8,000/8000) is the group doing the real specificity work here -- 'job'/'jobs' alone is broad, but combined with Meta AND the exact 8,000 figure it is not a realistic false-positive shape.
claims.source: research/scans/2026-09-17.json stats.dropped_candidates (meta-platforms (possible)); research/scans/2026-09-18.json stats.dropped_candidates (meta-platforms (possible)); research/digests/2026-09-18.md line 92 and 165 ('third consecutive cycle')
claims.notes: The 2026-09-18 digest and scan record both describe this as the claim's 'third cycle' / 'third consecutive cycle', but only two prior scan files (2026-09-17, 2026-09-18) are committed in research/scans/ with an itemized dropped_candidates record. No research/scans/2026-09-16.json exists. occurrences[] records only the two documented cycles; it is not stretched to three to match the prose claim.

claims.description: China's 'Ethnic Unity Law' actually passed 2026-03-12 per China's own official gazette. A recurring claim frames it as a September 2026 draft.
claims.claimed_framing: Implies the law is a September 2026 draft (specifically framed as an '8 September draft' in the 2026-09-15 cycle) rather than a law already passed in March.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the China entity token AND the distinctive 'Ethnic Unity Law' proper-noun phrase. Genuine, unrelated China news (trade policy, a different law, a different ethnic-policy story that does not use this specific name) will not match.

claims.description: PayPal's DOJ ~$30M DEI-related settlement was actually announced 2026-05-12, not in September. An undated aggregator snippet implied it was current.
claims.claimed_framing: Implies the DOJ DEI settlement is a fresh September 2026 development.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the PayPal entity token AND a DEI/diversity-equity topic token AND a settlement token, all three. A genuine PayPal settlement unrelated to DEI (e.g. a security or fraud settlement) or a genuine PayPal DEI story with no settlement (e.g. a policy change) will not match.
claims.notes: The forced-selection task brief that requested this ledger described this claim as recurring in a pattern parallel to Meta/China; the scan/digest records show only one documented occurrence so far (2026-09-18). occurrences[] reflects only what the committed records show.

claims.description: The Doha strike on ceasefire negotiators actually occurred 2025-09-09 (per a HRW/World Report 2026 country chapter), a year stale relative to a September 2026 scan window.
claims.claimed_framing: A 'Sept 9' mention inside a year-in-review-style source is read as September 2026 rather than the actual September 2025 event.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the Qatar/Doha entity token AND a strike-action token AND a negotiator/mediator/ceasefire target token. A genuine, unrelated Qatar strike story (e.g. a labor strike, an aviation incident) will not match because the negotiator/mediator/ceasefire token is absent.

claims.description: Freeport-McMoRan's Grasberg mine mud-rush fatality disclosure and related securities suit both date to September 2025 (press release dated 2025-09-24), a year stale relative to a September 2026 scan window.
claims.claimed_framing: Implies the Grasberg mud-rush fatality disclosure is a September 2026 event.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the Freeport-McMoRan/Grasberg entity token AND a mud-rush/fatality token. A genuine, unrelated Freeport-McMoRan story (earnings, a different safety incident) without fatality/mud-rush language will not match.

claims.description: The University of Cambridge protest injunction was actually granted 2025-03-21 (following the ELSC/Liberty intervention), over a year stale relative to a September 2026 scan window.
claims.claimed_framing: An undated recap is conflated with a current event, implying a September 2026 High Court escalation.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the exact 'university of cambridge' phrase (not just 'cambridge', which could also match a Cambridge, Massachusetts or Cambridge, UK city entity in the global-cities index) AND an injunction token AND a protest token. A genuine Cambridge (university or city) story without both an injunction and a protest will not match.

claims.description: Maduro's capture by US forces actually occurred 2026-01-03 through 2026-01-05 (source states a 3-5 January 2026 range); an undated search snippet read as current in September.
claims.claimed_framing: Implies the Maduro capture is a new September 2026 event.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the Venezuela/Maduro entity token AND a capture/arrest/detention token. A genuine, unrelated Venezuela or Maduro story (elections, sanctions, diplomacy) without a capture/arrest/detention framing will not match.
claims.notes: The forced-selection task brief that requested this ledger described this claim as 'first seen 2026-09-18'; the committed scan/digest records show it was actually first documented in the 2026-09-17 cycle's dropped_candidates, not 2026-09-18 (it does not reappear in the 2026-09-18 dropped_candidates list). first_seen/occurrences reflect the committed records, per the instruction not to invent a date.
